title: Vehicle as a Service (VaaS): Leverage Vehicles to Build Service Networks and Capabilities for Smart Cities
affiliation: University of Hong Kong, Shandong University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Case Western Reserve University, City University of Hong Kong
domain: Vehicular Edge Computing / Smart Cities / IoV / Mobile Edge Computing

analysis_policy.focus: Paradigm proposal extraction with emphasis on architectural design, service taxonomy, and integration with 5G+
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis including all 11 sections

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.summary: Introduces smart city vision through Alice scenario, identifies 5G+ cost limitations, and proposes VaaS as cost-effective alternative. Key insight: vehicles parked 23h/day with powerful SCCSI resources.
key_claims: 5G+ CAPEX and OPEX bottleneck commercial success
Vehicles will be SCCSI-empowered supercomputers on wheels (320-2000 TOPS)
VaaS reverses paradigm: vehicles as resource suppliers, not just consumers

section_flow.title: VaaS-Empowered Applications in Smart Cities
section_flow.summary: Presents application scenarios: crime detection via collaborative perception, HD map updates, traffic regulation, smart parking, connected healthcare, dining recommendations.
key_claims: VaaS enables city-wide safety net via citizen-contributed surveillance
Small proportion of autonomous vehicles can regulate traffic flow
24/7 health monitoring continuity across environments

section_flow.title: From VANETs to VaaS: What Upgrades Are Needed?
section_flow.summary: Identifies three upgrade requirements: spectrum perspective (CR for primary/secondary coexistence), computing perspective (safety-first resource harvesting), integrated SCCSI convergence.
key_claims: DSRC/C-V2X alone insufficient for crowdsourced services
Cognitive radio enables differentiated QoS guarantees
End-to-end service-oriented metrics require joint optimization

section_flow.title: The Architecture of the SCCSI Service Network
section_flow.summary: Proposes SCCSI service network: PoCs as mobile/fixed nodes with CR capabilities, SSP for centralized intelligence, SDN-based control plane, SCCSI resource map, incentive platform.
key_claims: PoC concept: SCCSI-equipped network connecting device (sensing + CR + computing + storage)
SSP provides C/U plane decoupling aligned with 5G+
VaaS extends 5G+ coverage to remote areas bridging digital divide

section_flow.title: Sensing as a Service
section_flow.summary: Reviews vehicular crowdsensing: multi-modal sensors (cameras, LiDAR, 4D radar), vehicle selection strategies, cooperative perception for communication-efficient data sharing, privacy-aware sensing.
key_claims: Tesla has 9 cameras; Mercedes/Honda introduced LiDAR in 2021
Task-oriented communication reduces sensing data via spatial confidence maps
Privacy preserved through feature extraction and differential privacy

section_flow.title: Communications as a Service
section_flow.summary: Reviews vehicular relay networks: parked vehicle mesh, platooning networks, position-based routing; store-carry-forward for content pushing and data mule operations.
key_claims: 5G NR V2X supports sidelink and UE relaying for multi-hop
Opportunistic content caching via passing vehicles reduces backhaul cost
120 taxis achieved 80% downtown coverage in 24h (Rome study)

section_flow.title: Computing as a Service
section_flow.summary: Reviews vehicular edge computing: NVIDIA DRIVE Thor (2000 TOPS), V2V offloading, device-to-vehicle offloading, parked vehicles as computing clusters, stopped vehicles at intersections.
key_claims: NVIDIA DRIVE Thor achieves 2000 TOPS for Level 5 autonomy
Electric vehicles can provide computing while charging
50% of US injury crashes occur at intersections - VaaS can help

section_flow.title: Storage as a Service
section_flow.summary: Reviews vehicular edge caching: reactive vs proactive caching, ICN for distributed content retrieval, LSTM-based travel time prediction for content placement.
key_claims: Autonomous vehicles generate up to 4TB/day requiring large storage
ICN enables anycasting robust to vehicle arrivals/departures
Centralized PoC can maintain lookup table for QoS guarantees

section_flow.title: Intelligence as a Service
section_flow.summary: Reviews vehicular FL and split learning: data-partition training (FL with vehicle selection), model-partition (split learning in platoons), collaborative inference for autonomous driving.
key_claims: Tesla Autopilot involves 48 neural networks
FL design must consider vehicle sojourn time and trajectory prediction
Split learning preferable for small dataset + large model

section_flow.title: Open Problems, Challenges, and Research Opportunities
section_flow.summary: Identifies research challenges: controllable PoC dispatch, service migration, digital twin integration, multi-hop task delivery, market-based incentives, ISAC, data privacy.
key_claims: UAV dispatch for edge computing is emerging hot topic
Joint sensing-communication-computing optimization needed
Differential privacy and secure aggregation critical for FL

section_flow.title: Conclusion
section_flow.summary: Summarizes VaaS vision as cost-effective complement to 5G+, emphasizes SCCSI convergence and paradigm shift from vehicles as consumers to suppliers.

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Open a position paper with a concrete user story that illustrates the envisioned paradigm before diving into technical details
structure: Create relatable character (Alice visiting city)
Walk through scenario with technology seamlessly integrated
Mention specific applications (localization, recommendation, autonomous driving, AR)
Transition: 'The above story is just a glimpse of...'
Define broader context and problem space
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Alice's smart city journey demonstrating VaaS capabilities
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Grounds abstract concepts in tangible user experience; creates emotional connection

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Frame a new paradigm by explicitly reversing the conventional perspective on a technology's role
structure: State conventional view (vehicles as END USERS)
Identify underutilized resources in conventional view (cars parked 23h/day)
Propose reversal (vehicles as RESOURCE SUPPLIERS)
Articulate implications of reversal
Coin memorable term (VaaS, SCCSI)
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: VaaS reverses vehicular networking from consumer-centric to supplier-centric

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Create a critical bridge section that identifies gaps between existing technology and envisioned paradigm
structure: Title: 'From X to Y: What Upgrades Are Needed?'
For each gap: State limitation → Explain why → Propose upgrade direction
Cover multiple perspectives (spectrum, computing, incentive)
Frame upgrades as design requirements for proposed architecture
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section III bridging VANETs to VaaS via CR, SCCSI integration, incentives
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Justifies need for proposed architecture; structures problem space
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium - requires deep understanding of existing limitations

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Organize a position paper around comprehensive service dimensions rather than technology components
structure: Define service dimensions (SCCSI: Sensing, Comms, Computing, Storage, Intelligence)
Dedicate equal sections to each dimension
Within each: state capability → review prior work → identify integration opportunities
Emphasize convergence and coupling across dimensions
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Sections V-IX covering SCCSI services with tight coupling emphasis
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Establishes comprehensive coverage; enables modular reading
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Medium-High - requires balanced depth across dimensions

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Include a timeline figure showing key technology milestones to contextualize capability evolution
structure: Identify key years with significant capability additions
For each milestone: company, product, specific capability metric
Focus on enabling technologies for proposed paradigm
Show progression toward envisioned capabilities
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Fig. 8: CAD milestones from Tesla cameras to NVIDIA DRIVE Thor 2000 TOPS
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Demonstrates technology maturity; provides evidence for timing

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Use a comprehensive comparison table to differentiate from prior surveys across multiple criteria
structure: List prior surveys/articles with year
Define distinguishing criteria as columns
Use checkmarks/crosses for binary coverage
Highlight comprehensive coverage of current work
Include 'Ours' row with all checkmarks
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Table I: 11 prior works × 5 criteria, only 'Ours' has all checkmarks
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Low-Medium - requires thorough related work analysis

key_concepts.PoC: Point of Connection - SCCSI-equipped network device installable on vehicles or fixed infrastructure
key_concepts.SSP: Secondary Service Provider - centralized entity managing VaaS with C/U plane decoupling
key_concepts.SCCSI_Service_Network: Integrated fixed + mobile infrastructure providing sensing, comms, computing, storage, intelligence services
